scope: Reverse command proof across temporary mobility/simulation loss; CBE source-level lifecycle review
finding: DrivingAssistRelease could retire the recovery journal while DrivingRecoveryRelease refused motion due to mobility/simulation/visibility. No exact command proof then remained for a later handback.
implementation: Retain otherwise exactly owned REVERSE work with releasePending=true and DEFERRED outcome while execution is unavailable.
Reconsider pending work from the existing DrivingAssistStart callback before recovery ownership evaluation or fresh assistance; reread work after release.
Revalidate route/seats/native tasks/external ownership in the existing unscheduled release transaction. New authority retires metadata without movement.
Do not replay a rear leg, refresh the original deadline, add callbacks/scanners, or republish an unchanged deferred state.
acceptanceRequired: Disable and re-enable simulation during an issued rear leg; require exact forward handback without another rear leg.
Immobilise and repair the same vehicle; verify original journal persists and new assistance follows handback.
Issue a new native STOP/MOVE, change seats/route or give Zeus/external control while unavailable; no stale command may be replayed.
Migrate vehicle/group ownership while pending; current owners must revalidate exact native command proof.
Keep driving disabled throughout reactivation and record absence of a guaranteed automatic observer rather than claiming success.
remaining: Physical vehicle/crew reactivation behaviour is unverified.
No independent observer when the whole driving subsystem is disabled; retained proof is not guaranteed timely cancellation.
Same-value external native orders remain indistinguishable without a cooperative ownership contract.
